## Table Without a Primary Key and 1st Normal Form (1NF)

## Short Answer: **No** (by strict definition)

---

## What 1NF Requires

1NF traditionally requires **all of the following**:

| Requirement | Description |
|---|---|
| **Atomic values** | Each column contains indivisible values |
| **No repeating groups** | No arrays or sets within a column |
| **Unique column names** | Each attribute has a distinct name |
| **Unique rows** | Each row must be uniquely identifiable (via **Primary Key**) |

---

## Why Primary Key Matters for 1NF

- Without a primary key, you can have **duplicate rows**
- Duplicate rows mean you **cannot uniquely identify** a record
- This violates the foundational relational principle defined by **Edgar F. Codd**

---

## Example of Violation

| Name | Age |
|---|---|
| Alice | 30 |
| Alice | 30 | ← duplicate row — violates 1NF |

---

## Note on Disagreement

Some modern interpretations focus **only on atomicity** for 1NF and treat the primary key as a **separate concern**, so opinions can vary depending on the source/textbook.

---

## Conclusion
By **strict/classical definition** → ❌ **Does NOT conform to 1NF** without a primary key.
